dependent_variable.name: CONACCi
dependent_variable.definition: Accrual-based conservatism proxy: the negative of the six-year mean of total accruals before depreciation, scaled by assets. Total accruals before depreciation are net income before extraordinary items plus depreciation expense less operating cash flows.
dependent_variable.formula: CONACCi = −mean_{1993–1998}[(NI before extraordinary items + depreciation expense − operating cash flows) / assets].

evidence.quote: Specifically, we use the sum of total accruals excluding depreciation (net income before extraordinary items plus depreciation expense less operating cash flows) deflated by assets and averaged within each of the two sample periods, 1993–1998 and 1987–1992, respectively, as our accrual-based proxy for conservatism.
We also multiply this measure by –1 so it is increasing in the amount of negative accruals, and refer to it as CONACC.

models.sample_description: Firm-year book-to-market panel for firms with book and market equity throughout 1993–1998, preceding six years of returns with dividends, and an S&P senior debt rating during the period. The source reports 730 qualifying firms; it does not report the number of firm-year regression rows.

models.equation_text: BTM_it = α + α_i + α_t + Σ_{k=0}^{6} β_k RET_{i,t−k} + e_it; (1).

fixed_effects.details: Separate firm-specific and year-specific fixed effects: α_i is the persistent firm bias component and α_t is the year component.

evidence.quote: with fixed firm and time effects
the persistent firm-specific bias component of book-to-market ratio over the sample period;
the year-specific component of book-to-market ratio across all firms;
Alpha is a common intercept;

estimation_procedure.description: Equation (1) is estimated with firm and year effects; the retained construction period is 1993–1998. CONMKT is the negative of the estimated firm-specific book-to-market component α_i.

evidence.quote: We perform the fixed-effects estimation separately on panel data for the two sample periods 1993–1998 and 1987–1992.
For ease of presentation we multiply �i by �1 and refer to this market-based proxy for conservatism as CONMKT.

sample_extraction.data_section_full_text:
Sample and Descriptive Statistics

We draw our sample from the 1998 Annual Industrial Compustat (Primary, Secondary,
and Tertiary) files. Our CONMKT conservatism measure derives from the fixed-effects
estimation of Equation (1) that requires that each firm have book and market values of
equity throughout each six-year period, 1993–1998 and 1987–1992. For each book-tomarket firm-year observation, we further require returns (with dividends) for the preceding
six years. We then estimate the fixed-effects model for those firms with an S&P senior debt
rating available on Compustat during the six-year period. The numbers of firms that meet
these data requirements are 730 and 593 in 1993–1998 and 1987–1992, respectively.

Cross-sectional (levels) analyses of conservatism and the cost of debt require additional
accounting and market variables as identified in Section IV. We obtain financial-statement
data from Compustat, and monthly stock returns for a minimum of 24 months of the sixyear sample periods from the 1998 CRSP database. These additional data requirements
reduce our sample of firms to 704 in 1993–1998, and 575 in 1987–1992, for our CONMKT
analysis. <sup>13</sup> For our CONACC analysis, additional financial statement data requirements reduce our sample to 632 firms in 1993–1998 and 517 firms in 1987–1992. Because we
estimate our conservatism measures over six-year windows, we similarly use the firmspecific mean value of each explanatory variable over the same six-year window in our
levels specification.

We further investigate these economic relations using a ‘‘changes’’ specification. For
each firm, we calculate changes in all variables as the firm-specific mean value for the
period 1993–1998 less the firm-specific mean value for the period 1987–1992. This differencing results in the loss of additional firms. Specifically, 568 and 484 firms have sufficient data for the changes specification using CONMKT and CONACC, respectively. Thus,
we perform all change analyses on these reduced samples.
